telos.statement: Determine which diagnostic decomposition most usefully explains the most material current Decision Lab UX/product failures, while staying faithful to Nicolas Bandurek's product feedback: move from selling feedback about mistakes to a goal-oriented managed-effort journey, make progress/KPI legible, reduce time-to-value, and preserve the unique statistical-to-personal value without making unsupported rating-improvement claims.
telos.success_condition: Compare the five audit prompts Truth/Perception/Action/Ownership/Effect against a stronger layered alternative on the frozen case corpus; identify where the alternative materially changes failure location, evidence request, or intervention; rank the highest-leverage product problems; and produce the smallest next product/field move that respects both Nico's commercial/product direction and the repository's evidence boundaries.

current_state.summary:
FROZEN INPUTS. Mentor source: Nicolas Bandurek meeting 2026-09-10. Nico's key product signals were: (N1) he struggled to understand the explanation and asked how the product moves from a generic statistical chess mistake to a personal mistake; generic mistakes were not interesting to him. (N2) the business question is 'I am 1500 and want to reach 2000; how do I do it?'; he said the product was selling the mistake instead of the player's advancement goal. (N3) he proposed 'managed effort': sell/manage the effort required to move from X toward Y rather than guarantee Y. (N4) he said 'you have not built KPI; until now you built feedback' and proposed a progress-bar layer plus a methodology of progress. (N5) he said the customer journey starts at the sale: rating X -> desired Y -> priced/managed effort -> app shows the path/effort, warns when the trajectory is off, and can renegotiate the goal. (N6) both sides recognized time-to-value as a real obstacle because personal inference may require roughly 60 decisions. Meeting summary recorded goal-oriented sales narrative, initial Chess.com 1200-1800 ICP, progress-bar KPI as core UI feature, and long time-to-value as a blocker. These are product/mentor signals, not evidence that rating improvement is caused by the app.

Frozen repository/product cases from current lichess_app PR #102 and its documented field/research findings:
C1 TIME_TO_VALUE_AND_WAITING: personal inference needs many decisions; the product repeatedly exposed internal readiness language such as variants of 'עוד 30 החלטות'. The history surface was over 4,000 CSS px before compression and remains long. The current learning layer explicitly does not render on an empty record, but calibration remains a real wait. Question: is the product presenting its instrument's need for evidence instead of the user's path toward improvement?
C2 FEEDBACK_WITHOUT_PROGRESS: Nico's strongest critique is that the product has feedback but no user-legible KPI/path. Current PR deliberately ships no global progress number, no rating denominator, and no prescribed programme because the discovery pipeline cannot establish causality/intervention/outcome; ratingSeries is stored but unrendered. A gate prevents rendering goal + count as an implied progress denominator. Question: what progress can legitimately be shown now without pretending calibration progress equals chess progress or rating causality?
C3 COLD_USERS_COULD_NOT_COMPLETE_MOVE: two cold testers independently could not complete a move. The sentence under the board named the position but not the act; the only 'choose a move' text was on a disabled submit below the fold. This was fixed in copy/layout but not yet field-validated after the fix. Question: does the five-part framework distinguish action selection from action execution enough to choose the right intervention/evidence?
C4 UNIQUE_VALUE_NOT_UNDERSTOOD: Nico repeatedly said he could not understand the focus until the explanation became 'how do we move from statistical mistake to personal mistake?' Current product/research value is precisely to distinguish player-specific-looking recurring structure from level-typical signal. Question: is this primarily Truth, Perception/representation, expected-value framing, or something else, and what should the product surface first?
C5 DETECTOR_SILENCE_VS_PERSON: the shipped six-bucket detector returned 'not-separable' on the owner's full record while the frozen research pipeline found a residual on that same record surviving its permutation null. Therefore 'no pattern cleared this detector' is true of the instrument but can be false as a description of the person. Question: what framework most reliably prevents instrument state from becoming a user identity claim?
C6 PROMPTED_TRANSFER_WAS_CALLED_TRANSFER: product logic had treated a player using their own rule on three prompted positions as 'transfer'. Research work separated guided practice, prompted recall/maximum transfer, and unprompted play/typical transfer. Question: where should internalization/ownership sit, and when is it even part of the product telos?
C7 JOURNEY_IS_MACHINERY_NOT_PATH: the product now has claims, drills, rules, retrieval queue, transfer tests, refutation and retirement, but these were reachable one at a time and not legible as one user journey. Nico's language is the inverse: the player should see the path/effort they need to traverse. Question: what is the minimum path representation that changes action now without inventing an unsupported programme?
C8 GOAL_PROGRESS_CAUSALITY_TRAP: a visual such as 1500 -> 1850 with 43% complete would satisfy Nico's goal framing but would imply a denominator/causal path the product has not established. Current repository gate rejects a goal rendered in the same element as a count when it would invite the reader to supply the arithmetic. Question: how can goal orientation and managed effort be respected without false progress?

Framework A under test: five audit prompts — Truth (what does the system actually know?), Perception (what does the user think it knows?), Action (what should the user do next?), Ownership (can the user carry/apply the distinction independently where transfer matters?), Effect (what actually changed?).
Framework B under test: layered fault-tree — Epistemic validity -> Representation/comprehension -> Action selection -> Action execution -> Internalization/transfer (only if required by telos) -> Outcome; motivation, expected value, trust, cost, ability and opportunity are modeled as moderators/bottlenecks rather than forced serial stages.

Comparison criterion: elegance does not count. B earns complexity only when it changes at least one of: failure location, evidence request, intervention, claim boundary, or priority. Nico fidelity means the final prioritization must explicitly address goal orientation, managed effort, KPI/progress, time-to-value, and statistical-to-personal value. Evidence fidelity means no promise of Elo/rating improvement, no progress denominator unsupported by data, and no claim that an unvalidated fix is easier for users.
known_constraints: Treat Nico's statements as high-value product/mentor signals, not empirical proof of user behavior or rating causality.
Do not reinterpret 'progress bar' literally if that would imply unsupported causal distance to a rating goal.
Distinguish calibration/evidence progress, managed effort/adherence, skill-process change, and external rating outcome.
Do not collapse action selection with action execution.
Do not collapse prompted performance with unprompted transfer.
Ownership/internalization is conditional on telos, not universal.
Do not call the cold-user fix validated until FIELD evidence confirms it.
Judge the frameworks by discrimination power, not memorability or MECE aesthetics.
Prefer the smallest reversible next move that can change a product decision.

decision_blocked.statement: Which current UX/product failures should be treated as the highest-leverage bottlenecks, what diagnostic distinctions actually matter, and what should Decision Lab build/test next if it follows Nico's managed-effort/product-journey insight without violating the repository's evidence boundaries?
decision_blocked.current_default: Do not build a literal rating progress bar or full prescribed coaching programme. Use the five prompts only provisionally, and prioritize a truthful journey/progress representation plus field validation only if the paired comparison shows those distinctions change the next move.
decision_blocked.reversal_condition: Change the default if the paired comparison shows that a more specific layered diagnosis leads to materially different, lower-risk interventions or evidence requests on the frozen cases, especially around time-to-value, KPI/progress, action execution, statistical-to-personal value, and transfer.

signals: Nico's strongest product delta was 'you built feedback; you have not built KPI'.
Nico framed the product as managed effort toward a user-selected goal, not as a mistake-reporting tool.
The repository independently found that its machinery was mostly built but invisible as one journey.
The repository also forbids a naive goal denominator because causal progress toward rating has not been established.

The key product design problem may therefore be representing a truthful path whose progress units are evidence collection, effort/adherence, and target-process change rather than invented percent-to-rating.
The paired test should reveal whether this conclusion comes from the five prompts or requires the layered distinctions.
